.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r4/task/tests/scoring.toml, task/tests/tools/score.py, task/tests/Dockerfile (rewardkit 0.1.7), task/instruction.md (grep for visual/craft wording)
evidence: Type assignment matches the nature of each ask. (1) Gates: task/tests/gates/render/judge.toml:20 and gates/constraints/judge.toml:20 are type="binary" (hro_gate_render, hro_gate_shared), as the contract requires (staged-task-contract.md:96 'Gates stay at 0.0 and their criteria stay binary'); scoring.toml [gates] render/constraints=0.0. (2) Functional: all 41 criteria in task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml (lines 26..404, hro_job_open .. hro_restart) are type="binary" with positive weights 0.5-2.5; each is a concrete pass/fail product rule (refusals, reorder, undo, unread counts, privacy, restart). Grep for degree words (quality|well|nice|clean|good|appropriate|reasonabl) in functional/gate judge.toml returned nothing, so no craft judgement is hidden in a binary row. (3) Polish: 5 criteria, all type="binary" (polish/judge.toml:20,29,38,47,56). polish/prompt.md:14 says 'Judge how the workspace holds up while people work at the same time, not visual craft'; each row is a concrete preservation/refusal behaviour with explicit failure conditions (draft value, document.activeElement, scroll offset, getBoundingClientRect within a few pixels, no double send, sign-in prompt, per-user drafts) - pass/fail, so binary fits and no gradation is lost. (4) Visual: all 5 craft criteria (hro_vis_type/color/layout/hierarchy/consistency, visual/judge.toml:20-21,35-36,50-51,65-66,80-81) are type="likert", points=5, weight 1.2, and every one carries a described anchor at each of 5,4,3,2,1 (e.g. judge.toml:25-29 typography; 40-44 colour; 55-59 layout; 70-74 hierarchy; 85-89 consistency). No likert block lacks an anchor; no craft criterion is binary. Scale consistency: the template visual uses a 0-5 anchor set and its prompt notes RewardKit renders 'an integer from 1 to 5' (template visual/prompt.md:34-42); the task instead uses 1-5 anchors, which agrees with that RewardKit schema hint, and every task prompt states the lowest score consistently ('binary 0; Likert 1', functional/polish/gates prompt.md:7; visual/prompt.md:12,16 'minimum raw Likert score 1, which normalizes to zero'). The Internal annotation ('Likert we dont use in rewardkit') is the documented known false positive (SKILL.md 'Likert versus weighted'); judged against the shipped format, which is the template's own likert visual dimension. Adversarial probes: (a) a broken/craft-only app - a beautiful static shell cannot earn behavioural credit through likert because all behaviour rows are binary and the gates/functional floor (scoring.toml floors functional=0.05; score.py gates_passed) zero it; within visual the in-dimension gate sends it to Likert 1. (b) a conforming alternative that could be under-scored by type choice - e.g. an app whose concurrent-edit preservation is correct but whose look differs from the golden: polish is binary on observable state, not style, and visual anchors are style-neutral ('Layout, labels and styles are the implementer's choice', visual/prompt.md:14), so neither type choice penalizes it. Neither probe exposes a type/anchor misfit. Residual, outside this row's verdict: rewardkit 0.1.7 is not installed locally and raw-evidence-index.json lists no configured judge run, so the claim that raw Likert 1 normalizes to exactly 0 was not measured here (relevant to rows 39/40/42, not to type fit). Also noted for the owner: frozen rules/'WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx' sha256 6d44970b... differs from the skill asset WebDev_Rubrics_QC.xlsx d7b5d607...; row 41 text read in the frozen rules copy was used.
